type: sharpened free-component bound — theory, light compute, ledgers unchanged

s1_s10_geometry.statement: the free target of an entry with rotation length ell is u -> T1(sigma^ell(u))
s1_s10_geometry.ell5: equals tau(u): same E-orbit, phase +1, last letter preserved (720/720 words)
s1_s10_geometry.ell_lt_5: leaves the E-orbit for EVERY word and every ell < 5 (0/720 stay)
s1_s10_geometry.consequence: short passes are exactly the orbit-changing free arcs

s2_merging_efficiency.proof: a short pass changes exactly one vertex's out-arc; adding one arc reduces the weak-component count by at most 1, so m(d) = 1 for every deficit d

s12_short_pass_count.per_hexagon_shortfall_identity: sum over the passes of hexagon h of (5 - ell) = 6(e_h - 1)
s12_short_pass_count.consequence: if e_h >= 2 then ALL e_h passes of h are short (sum ell = 6 - e_h <= 4)
s12_short_pass_count.formula: #short = F + m, with m = #{h : e_h >= 2} <= F

s5_s6_path_cover.theorem: non-free arcs >= p(G0) - 1, where p is the minimum vertex-disjoint directed path cover of G0
s5_s6_path_cover.proof: the free arcs used by the Hamiltonian path form a vertex-disjoint path system covering V, so |free_used| <= V - p, hence non-free >= (V-1) - (V-p) = p - 1
s5_s6_path_cover.exact_formula_for_outdegree_le_1: p = I0 + Z_bare, where I0 = #vertices of in-degree 0 and Z_bare = #components that are bare cycles (no in-trees attached)
s5_s6_path_cover.relation: p >= c always; p > c exactly when G0 branches (two entries sharing a free target)
s5_s6_path_cover.branching_requires_short_passes: at F = 0 all arcs are tau-arcs and tau is injective, so in-degree <= 1 and p = c: NO GAIN in the F=0 column

sharpened_component_bound.derivation: baseline tau-graph on the 120+F entries has >= O = 24+k components; each of the <= 2F short passes can merge at most one pair

s9_tradeoff_REFUTED.claim: F + c(G0) >= 29 for every NR6 walk
s9_tradeoff_REFUTED.counterexample: this repository's own greedy n=6 superpermutation: L=873, F=0, c(G0)=24, F+c = 24 < 29
s9_tradeoff_REFUTED.also_fails_for_path_cover: p = c = 24 on the same walk, so the path-cover refinement does not rescue the tradeoff
s9_tradeoff_REFUTED.note: F + c >= 29 is sufficient for L >= 872 but is NOT necessary; a walk of length 873 sits at 24, so the inequality cannot be proved universally

s7_f0_calibration.F0_structure: every pass full, G0 = tau restricted to entries, c >= O = 24 + k
s7_f0_calibration.at_k0: L >= 867 — this is exactly the Houston bound, re-derived

exact_cover_test.question: do 24 E-orbits partition the 120 hexagons exactly?
exact_cover_test.consequence: the (0,0) cell cannot be eliminated this way

s8_872_positive_control.note: the witness is never rejected; the bound meets it with equality

diagnosis_of_the_missing_five.finding: on BOTH real walks the arc-COUNT bound S >= c - 1 is EXACTLY TIGHT (872 witness: S=3=c-1; greedy 873: S=23=c-1)
diagnosis_of_the_missing_five.gap_source: the entire residual cost is H — heavy joints of weight >= 4. greedy 873 pays 29 = 23 + 6 with four weight-4 joints and one weight-5 joint
diagnosis_of_the_missing_five.conclusion: the free-arc structure determines the NUMBER of non-free arcs perfectly but is blind to their WEIGHT. Reaching 872 from 867 requires forcing H >= 5 - k in the F = 0 column — a statement about hub defects, not about G0.
diagnosis_of_the_missing_five.restated_open_statement: for every NR6 walk with F = 0: H + (c - (24+k)) >= 5 - k

s13_cells.reason: the sharpened bound raises F + c only to 24 + k - F, whose maximum over the feasible cells is 28 at (k,F) = (4,0), one short of 29

disclaimer: This project has not proved L6 >= 872.
